paragraphs: Friend, this one is heavy, so I'll say it plain. God tells Ezekiel to write down the date, because on that very day the king of Babylon laid siege to Jerusalem (Ezekiel 24:2). God sees what's happening before any news travels. Nothing about this hour caught Him off guard.

Now look at the pot. God says the city is a pot "now rusted, whose rust will not come off!" (Ezekiel 24:6). Then He says, "Because of the indecency of your uncleanness I tried to cleanse you, but you would not be purified from your filthiness." (Ezekiel 24:13). I think that's the tender part hiding inside the hard part. God tried to clean it first, and the fire came after the cleaning didn't take.

So here's what I'd carry out of this kitchen, baker. God means what He says, and He says "I will judge you according to your ways and deeds" (Ezekiel 24:14). Don't shrug off the little rust spots, because He sees them, and He has said He will not relent. I spent years in a dusty drawer, and I'm telling you, the One who sees us clearly is the One we want to listen to.
